jp: {もし|av-moshi}宝[たから]くじが当[あ]たったら、世界[せかい]一周[いっしゅう]の旅[たび]に出[で]たいです。
en: If I won the lottery, I would like to set off on a trip around the world.
why: もし opens an ordinary hypothetical that is answered with たら; たとえ needs ても and まるで needs ようだ.

jp: {もし|av-moshi}明日[あした]雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ったら、試合[しあい]は中止[ちゅうし]になります。
en: If it rains tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
why: A plain if-clause with たら is introduced by もし; たとえ would demand ても.

jp: {もし/万一[まんいち]|av-moshi}道[みち]に迷[まよ]ったら、この番号[ばんごう]に電話[でんわ]してください。
en: If you should get lost, please call this number.
why: もし (or 万一 for a worst case) introduces the if-clause; the others cannot go with たら.

jp: {もし|av-moshi}分[わ]からないことがあれば、いつでも聞[き]いてください。
en: If there is anything you don't understand, please ask me any time.
why: もし sets up a neutral condition with ば; たとえ would require ても and きっと cannot start an if-clause.

jp: {もし/仮[かり]に|av-moshi}私[わたし]があなたの立場[たちば]なら、その話[はなし]は断[ことわ]ります。
en: If I were in your position, I would turn that offer down.
why: A hypothetical "if I were you" with なら is opened by もし (or 仮に); たとえ would need ても.

jp: {もし|av-moshi}時間[じかん]があれば、一緒[いっしょ]に買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]きませんか。
en: If you have time, shall we go shopping together?
why: もし introduces a simple condition with ば; たとえ and まるで do not fit an if-clause.

jp: {もし/仮[かり]に|av-moshi}一人[ひとり]で行[い]くなら、バスより電車[でんしゃ]のほうが便利[べんり]ですよ。
en: If you are going alone, the train is more convenient than the bus.
why: もし goes with なら to open a condition; たとえ would require ても.

jp: {万一[まんいち]/もし|av-moshi}火事[かじ]になったら、すぐに非常口[ひじょうぐち]から逃[に]げてください。
en: In the unlikely event of a fire, please escape at once through the emergency exit.
why: 万一 stresses a worst case that is very unlikely; it takes たら, whereas たとえ takes ても.

jp: {万一[まんいち]/もし|av-moshi}財布[さいふ]をなくしたら、すぐカード会社[かいしゃ]に連絡[れんらく]します。
en: If, by any chance, I lose my wallet, I will contact the card company immediately.
why: 万一 introduces an unwelcome possibility with たら; たとえ would need ても.

jp: {万一[まんいち]/もし|av-moshi}遅[おく]れるようなことがあれば、必[かなら]ず連絡[れんらく]します。
en: If by some chance I should be late, I will be sure to let you know.
why: 万一 marks a remote, undesirable possibility and goes with ば; the other adverbs do not.

jp: {万一[まんいち]/もし|av-moshi}地震[じしん]が起[お]きたら、この広場[ひろば]に集[あつ]まることになっています。
en: If an earthquake should happen, we are supposed to gather in this square.
why: A feared but unlikely event with たら takes 万一; たとえ would need ても.

jp: {万一[まんいち]/もし|av-moshi}間違[まちが]いがあれば、すぐ教[おし]えてください。
en: If there should be any mistake, please tell me right away.
why: 万一 marks an unlikely problem with ば; たとえ and まるで cannot open this clause.

jp: {万一[まんいち]/もし|av-moshi}ここで事故[じこ]が起[お]きたら、大[おお]きな問題[もんだい]になる。
en: If an accident should happen here, it would become a big problem.
why: An unlikely accident with たら is introduced by 万一; たとえ would require ても.

jp: {仮[かり]に/もし|av-moshi}この話[はなし]が本当[ほんとう]だとしたら、すぐに調[しら]べる必要[ひつよう]がある。
en: Supposing this story is true, we need to look into it right away.
why: 仮に means "suppose that" and fits だとしたら; たとえ would need ても.

jp: {仮[かり]に/もし|av-moshi}明日[あした]から休[やす]みがもらえるなら、どこへ行[い]きますか。
en: Suppose you could get time off starting tomorrow, where would you go?
why: 仮に sets up an imagined situation with なら; たとえ would need ても.

jp: {仮[かり]に/もし|av-moshi}給料[きゅうりょう]が二倍[にばい]になれば、生活[せいかつ]はずっと楽[らく]になるだろう。
en: Supposing my salary doubled, life would become a lot easier.
why: 仮に introduces a supposition completed by ば; たとえ would require ても.

jp: {仮[かり]に/もし|av-moshi}あなたが社長[しゃちょう]だったら、どうしますか。
en: Suppose you were the company president, what would you do?
why: A counterfactual supposition with たら is opened by 仮に (or もし); たとえ needs ても.

jp: {仮[かり]に/もし|av-moshi}百万円[ひゃくまんえん]が手[て]に入[はい]ったら、何[なに]に使[つか]いますか。
en: Supposing you got a million yen, what would you spend it on?
why: 仮に sets up an imagined case with たら; たとえ would force ても.

jp: {仮[かり]に/もし/万一[まんいち]|av-moshi}計画[けいかく]が失敗[しっぱい]したら、責任[せきにん]は誰[だれ]が取[と]るのですか。
en: Supposing the plan fails, who will take responsibility?
why: 仮に opens a supposition with たら; たとえ would require ても.

jp: もし明日[あした]天気[てんき]が{よかったら/よければ/いいなら|av-moshi}、公園[こうえん]でお弁当[べんとう]を食[た]べましょう。
en: If the weather is nice tomorrow, let's eat a packed lunch in the park.
why: もし calls for a conditional ending; ても would mean "even if" and ので/のに state facts.

jp: もし分[わ]からない言葉[ことば]が{あったら/あれば|av-moshi}、辞書[じしょ]を引[ひ]いてみてください。
en: If there are any words you don't understand, try looking them up in a dictionary.
why: もし requires a conditional (たら/ば); ても, ので and のに give the wrong meaning.

jp: もし私[わたし]が{鳥[とり]なら/鳥[とり]だったら|av-moshi}、あの山[やま]を越[こ]えて飛[と]んでいくのに。
en: If I were a bird, I would fly over that mountain.
why: A counterfactual wish begun by もし takes なら or たら; ても would mean "even if".

jp: もし道[みち]が{込[こ]んでいたら/込[こ]んでいれば|av-moshi}、電車[でんしゃ]で行[い]きましょう。
en: If the road is crowded, let's go by train.
why: もし is completed by a conditional form; ても, ので and のに break the logic.

jp: もし京都[きょうと]へ{行[い]くなら/行[い]ったら|av-moshi}、清水寺[きよみずでら]を見[み]るといいですよ。
en: If you are going to Kyoto, you should see Kiyomizu-dera.
why: もし begins a conditional; 行っても would mean "even if you go" and the others state facts.

jp: もし疲[つか]れて{いたら/いれば|av-moshi}、無理[むり]をしないで休[やす]んでください。
en: If you are tired, please don't push yourself and rest.
why: もし is followed by a conditional; ても would mean "even if you are tired", changing the advice.

jp: もし車[くるま]を{買[か]うなら|av-moshi}、小[ちい]さいのがいいです。
en: If I buy a car, I would like a small one.
why: もし goes with a conditional; ても, ので and のに do not express "if".

jp: もし五分[ごふん]早[はや]く{出[で]ていれば/出[で]ていたら|av-moshi}、電車[でんしゃ]に間[ま]に合[あ]ったのに。
en: If we had left five minutes earlier, we would have caught the train.
why: A counterfactual about the past uses もし with ていれば/ていたら; ても would make "even if", which contradicts 間に合った.

jp: もし日本語[にほんご]が{話[はな]せれば/話[はな]せたら|av-moshi}、日本[にほん]で働[はたら]きたいです。
en: If I could speak Japanese, I would like to work in Japan.
why: もし requires a conditional ending; ても, ので and のに do not state a condition.

jp: もし来週[らいしゅう]{ひまなら/ひまだったら|av-moshi}、一緒[いっしょ]に映画[えいが]を見[み]に行[い]きませんか。
en: If you are free next week, shall we go and see a film together?
why: もし is answered by なら or だったら; ひまでも means "even if free" and the others state facts.

jp: もし値段[ねだん]が{安[やす]ければ/安[やす]かったら|av-moshi}、二[ふた]つ買[か]います。
en: If the price is low, I will buy two.
why: もし introduces a conditional; 安くても means "even if cheap", which makes no sense here.

jp: もし私[わたし]に電話[でんわ]が{あったら/あれば|av-moshi}、会議中[かいぎちゅう]だと伝[つた]えてください。
en: If there is a call for me, please tell them I'm in a meeting.
why: もし goes with a conditional; ても, ので and のに do not mean "if".

jp: 万一[まんいち]けがを{したら/すれば|av-moshi}、すぐに係[かかり]の人[ひと]に知[し]らせてください。
en: If you should get hurt, please tell the staff member right away.
why: 万一 requires a conditional ending; しても would mean "even if you get hurt".

jp: 仮[かり]に彼[かれ]の言[い]うとおり{なら/だったら|av-moshi}、私[わたし]たちの負[ま]けだ。
en: Supposing it is as he says, we lose.
why: 仮に sets up a supposition that ends in なら or だったら; the others do not express "if".

jp: 仮[かり]に今[いま]すぐ{出発[しゅっぱつ]すれば/出発[しゅっぱつ]したら|av-moshi}、夕方[ゆうがた]までに着[つ]けるでしょう。
en: Supposing we leave right now, we should be able to arrive by evening.
d: 出発[しゅっぱつ]しても
出発[しゅっぱつ]したので
出発[しゅっぱつ]するのに
why: 仮に takes a conditional; 出発しても would mean "even if we leave", which contradicts 着けるでしょう.
